key_insight: An infrastructure-first, prior-conditioned segmentation pipeline detects CAFO infrastructure (barns, lagoons, feedlots) from aerial and satellite imagery and assembles those components into explainable CAFO footprints at scale.
problem_solved: Provides accurate, scalable and interpretable mapping of Concentrated Animal Feeding Operations from remote-sensing data—addressing gaps in surveillance, environmental monitoring, and risk assessment caused by fragmented or opaque detection methods.
method: Prior-conditioned segmentation: incorporate infrastructure priors (shape, spatial relationships, contextual cues) to guide models toward CAFO-relevant features in aerial/satellite imagery.
Infrastructure-first assembly: segment component classes (e.g., barns, waste lagoons, pens, access roads) and link them into CAFO footprints and attribute records.
Explainable, scalable pipeline: produce per-component confidence/uncertainty, human-interpretable outputs, and tile-based inference for large-area mapping.
impact: Shows how domain priors and component-level modeling improve performance and interpretability of remote-sensing segmentation pipelines, offering a transferable pattern for AI practitioners building operational, policy-relevant mapping systems.
visual_elements: Side-by-side imagery: raw aerial/satellite image vs. overlaid component segmentation (barns, lagoons, pens) and assembled CAFO footprint.
Pipeline diagram: flowchart illustrating prior-conditioning → component segmentation → footprint assembly → explainability/uncertainty outputs.
Icon grid: representative icons for detected infrastructure types with per-class confidence scores.
Scalability chart: map tiles processed over area vs. precision/recall or throughput, showing operational coverage.
paper_title: PRISM-CAFO: Prior-conditioned Remote-sensing Infrastructure Segmentation and Mapping for CAFOs
paper_authors: Oishee Bintey Hoque, Nibir Chandra Mandal, Kyle Luong, Amanda Wilson, Samarth Swarup
